text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Tuesday morning newspapers:
- Opposition centre-right Social Democrats said they will demand a no-confidence vote against the government on Tuesday after it failed to send the budget to parliament on Monday.
- Ministry of Economic Activities said it will invest $140 million for the modernisation and raising capacity of Slovenia's oil refinery Nafta Lendava.
- According to first estimates, hail in the southern region of Dolenjska on Monday destroyed between 30 and 100 percent of all crops.
- Marc Vienot, general director of French bank Societe Generale, visted Slovenian president Milan Kucan and the governor of the central bank France Arhar on Monday.
- Governmental coalition parties on Monday agreed on Slovenia's maximum budget for this year to be at 730 billion tolars ($4.5 billion), Marjan Podobnik, vice president of the government said.
- Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler denied unofficial talk that he intended to resign.
